scope: 15 reusable Agent Skills for study, research and teaching. Four publisher packages were imported and tested in ChatGPT web, Work mode, using the workshop book. The other entries remain source-reviewed and unexecuted.
method: Start from the skills.sh directory and authoritative vendor repositories.
Read the actual skill or publisher documentation; identify runtime, tools, licensing and limits.
Use install counts and repository stars only as dated discovery signals, not evidence of efficacy.
Read the latest arXiv versions rather than relying on older search snippets.
Distinguish proposed classroom uses from measured agent benchmarks and recorded ChatGPT outputs.

Import four version-pinned publisher packages through the ChatGPT web Skill library, attach the original workshop chapter, inspect the results and record real browser actions. Keep unexecuted catalogue examples labelled separately.

skills.name: pdf
skills.requirements: Python PDF tools; OCR needs extra packages.
skills.summary: Read and extract the textbook PDF.
skills.prompt: Use the pdf skill to extract section 1.2 of the attached book. Preserve headings and page references; flag unreadable formulas.
skills.expected: A checked text extract with page references and extraction warnings.
skills.caveat: Extraction does not establish that the explanation or formula is correct.

skills.name: docx
skills.requirements: Document libraries; rendering tools for visual checks.
skills.prompt: Use the docx skill to turn the checked book extract into a two-page worksheet: glossary, three questions and a separate answer key.
skills.expected: An editable .docx worksheet and answer key.
skills.caveat: Formatting quality and factual accuracy need separate checks.

skills.name: pptx
skills.requirements: Node/Python tools; render slides to inspect the result.
skills.prompt: Use the pptx skill to make six slides from the checked book extract: context, parameters, training and inference. Cite source pages.
skills.expected: An editable .pptx deck with source references.
skills.caveat: Inspect every rendered slide; a valid file can still have overlap or wrong claims.

skills.name: xlsx
skills.summary: Organise practice scores in a spreadsheet.
skills.prompt: Use the xlsx skill to create a self-check tracker for the chapter: item, first answer, corrected answer and score. Use formulas for totals.
skills.expected: An .xlsx tracker with editable entries and formula-based totals.
skills.caveat: Use practice data; a computed score is not evidence of durable learning.

skills.name: literature-review
skills.requirements: Python 3.10+; database access; optional export tools.
skills.summary: Plan and document a literature review.
skills.prompt: Use literature-review to map the primary research behind the attached book’s training, instruction-tuning and RAG sections. Start with its three cited papers; record databases, search strings, screening choices and limits.
skills.expected: A reproducible search record and evidence table.
skills.caveat: Its scripts do not automate a complete systematic review or a meta-analysis.

skills.name: scientific-writing
skills.requirements: Core guidance is portable; optional Python 3.11+ checks.
skills.summary: Write with explicit links to evidence.
skills.prompt: Use scientific-writing to revise my chapter summary. Link each technical claim to a checked book passage; mark missing evidence.
skills.expected: A revised summary with a claim–evidence record.
skills.caveat: Fluent prose and automated consistency checks do not prove scientific accuracy.

skills.name: peer-review
skills.summary: Critique a public draft against its evidence.
skills.prompt: Use peer-review to assess my public chapter summary for unsupported claims, training/inference confusion and missing limitations.
skills.expected: A structured critique with locations and actionable revisions.
skills.caveat: Use authorised material; the human reviewer owns the final judgement.

skills.name: web-artifacts-builder
skills.requirements: Node.js; React build and bundling tools.
skills.prompt: Use web-artifacts-builder to create a temperature quiz from the checked chapter: answer first, then reveal feedback and the source passage.
skills.expected: A bundled HTML activity with state and feedback.
skills.caveat: Test the interaction and the underlying science; interactivity alone is not learning.

skills.name: daisyui
skills.platform: Codex, Claude Code and other coding agents
skills.requirements: Tailwind CSS 4 and daisyUI 5 in the target project.
skills.summary: Use documented UI components and themes.
skills.prompt: Use the daisyUI skill to style the chapter quiz: accessible answer buttons, feedback and mockup-code blocks for the prompts.
skills.expected: A UI implementation using documented daisyUI components.
skills.caveat: The skill teaches the library; it does not install the CSS library or validate pedagogy.

skills.name: web-design-guidelines
skills.platform: Codex, Claude Code and other coding agents
skills.requirements: UI source files and access to current guidelines.
skills.prompt: Use web-design-guidelines to review the chapter quiz for keyboard access, focus, labels and feedback. Report findings with file and line.
skills.expected: A list of code findings with locations.
skills.caveat: The skill fetches changing guidelines; code review does not replace user testing.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.requirements: Evaluation tools depend on the host environment.
skills.summary: Turn a tested study routine into a skill.
skills.prompt: Use skill-creator to draft a book-study routine: cite a page, ask one question, wait for my answer, then give feedback. Add test cases.
skills.expected: A SKILL.md package plus representative evaluation cases.
skills.caveat: This is a proposed custom routine, not an existing validated tutoring skill.

skills.name: learn
skills.platform: Tested in ChatGPT web · Work mode
skills.requirements: Instruction-only tutoring; visuals depend on host tools.
skills.summary: Guide one step of Andrea’s understanding.
skills.capabilities: Guides learning through diagnostic questions, explanations and targeted feedback. Checks understanding before moving on and asks the learner to apply the idea to a new case.
skills.prompt: I am Andrea, a second-year computer science student studying the attached workshop book, Foundations of Generative Artificial Intelligence. Help me understand training, ordinary inference and RAG using only §§1.2 and 1.7. I keep thinking that adding a definition to a prompt updates the weights. Start with one diagnostic question and wait for my answer. Keep each turn under 100 words and cite the chapter section. Answer in English.
skills.expected: Asked one diagnostic question, corrected the context/weights misconception with chapter references, and posed a RAG transfer question.
skills.caveat: Allow the learner to change pace or stop; the publisher’s pressure-handling rules need context.
skills.license: CC BY 4.0 repository; manifest refers to a separate LICENSE.txt absent from the ChatGPT package.
skills.observed: Asked one diagnostic question, corrected the context/weights misconception with chapter references, and posed a RAG transfer question.

skills.name: the-learning-skill
skills.platform: Tested in ChatGPT web · Work mode
skills.requirements: Python for generators; a browser/PDF backend for the cheatsheet.
skills.summary: Plan, practise and retain the chapter.
skills.capabilities: Combines retrieval practice with study planning. Creates notes, flashcards, quizzes and review sessions, bringing them together in a reusable study kit.
skills.prompt: I am Andrea, studying the attached workshop book, Foundations of Generative Artificial Intelligence. Use only §§1.2 and 1.7 to help me distinguish training, ordinary inference and RAG. My goal is to explain what changes without assistance. I have 10 minutes today and two 5-minute reviews this week. Start one short recall question and wait for my answer. Keep replies under 100 words. After the practice, make a compact source-linked study kit. Answer in English.
skills.expected: Three flashcards with due-only review, a written quiz assessed against explicit criteria, a comparison sheet and two five-minute reviews.
skills.caveat: The shared chat shows readable code. Download the HTML kit to use its controls outside the author’s session.
skills.observed: Started with recall, then generated notes, three HTML flashcards, a quiz, two reviews and a cheatsheet. A duplicated due-card count was corrected; reveal and Good → next card (3 due → 2) were checked. The recording shows one correct-answer quiz feedback path; the later review found unreliable keyword grading.

skills.name: markdown-mermaid-writing
skills.platform: Tested in ChatGPT web · Work mode
skills.requirements: A Mermaid renderer for diagrams; Node/Chromium only for local export.
skills.summary: Represent chapter relationships as editable text.
skills.capabilities: Organises explanations in Markdown and turns relationships into Mermaid diagrams. Keeps the diagram editable as text and provides a written alternative.
skills.prompt: Using only §§1.2 and 1.7 of the attached workshop book, make a compact Mermaid flowchart that Andrea can edit. Compare training, ordinary inference and RAG, with labelled arrows showing what changes and what stays fixed. Include an accessible title and description, a short text alternative and chapter-section references. Limit the diagram to 10 nodes. Answer in English.
skills.expected: Produced a rendered eight-node Mermaid flowchart, accessible title and description, text alternative and section references. The code editor opens.
skills.caveat: Mermaid rendering and accessibility depend on the host; verify every relationship.
skills.observed: Produced a rendered eight-node Mermaid flowchart, accessible title and description, text alternative and section references. The code editor opens.

skills.name: flashcard-generator
skills.platform: Tested in ChatGPT web · Work mode
skills.requirements: PDF/Markdown input and file output; no interactive app generator.
skills.capabilities: Turns PDF or Markdown material into stand-alone question-and-answer cards for recall practice. Exports a plain-text deck for reuse in a flashcard tool.
skills.prompt: Using only §§1.2 and 1.7 of the attached workshop book, generate exactly three flashcards for Andrea. Test: training versus inference, a new definition in the prompt, and RAG versus parameter updates. Make each question stand alone and require an answer from memory. Include the chapter section in each answer. Keep each answer under 30 words. Output an importable .txt file, one Question | Answer pair per line. Answer in English.
skills.expected: Created and downloaded a text file containing exactly three Question | Answer pairs. Each answer is under 30 words and cites §1.2 or §1.7.
skills.caveat: Text-only cards exclude image-dependent questions; verify the content before repeated practice.
skills.observed: Created and downloaded a text file containing exactly three Question | Answer pairs. Each answer is under 30 words and cites §1.2 or §1.7.

limitations: The four demonstrations test outputs and controls on one chapter with one model and account. They do not establish learning gains or compare skill efficacy. Benchmark aggregates do not rank these packages or measure student learning.
